beginner.headline: Romesh and Sebastian Win The Celebrity Traitors
beginner.brief: The second series of The Celebrity Traitors ended on Friday. More than 15 million people watched the series. There were 21 players at the start, but only seven reached the last show. Romesh Ranganathan and Sebastian Croft won the game together. They shared a prize of £83,000. The winners will give the money to two charities, groups that help people in need. Sebastian cried because he was very happy. Romesh hoped his mum was proud of him.

intermediate.headline: Romesh Ranganathan and Sebastian Croft Win Celebrity Traitors
intermediate.brief: The second series of BBC One's The Celebrity Traitors reached its final on Friday. For four weeks, famous contestants faced suspense and suspicion as they tried to win through clever thinking. More than 15 million people have been watching this series. The group of 21 original contestants was reduced to seven before the final. Comedian Romesh Ranganathan and actor Sebastian Croft became the two winners, both belonging to the team called the faithful. The faithful team succeeded in removing the remaining traitors, Maya Jama and King Kenny, and the winners shared £83,000 for charity. During the final stage, contestants gathered around a fire pit to decide whether any traitors were still in the game. After a tied vote between James Blunt and Kenny, Croft persuaded Ranganathan to vote Kenny out, securing victory for the faithful. James then chose another round of voting and was removed himself, leaving Ranganathan and Croft as the final two. James could have shared the win if he had chosen to finish the game, as Ranganathan and Croft did. The winners will divide their money between two refugee charities, the Refugee Council and Choose Love.

advanced.headline: Celebrity Traitors Finale Delivers Victory Amid Mixed Reactions
advanced.brief: Some of Britain's biggest stars spent four weeks engaged in a battle of wits on The Celebrity Traitors. By Friday's final, the original field of 21 celebrities had been whittled down to seven. Comedian Romesh Ranganathan and Heartstopper actor Sebastian “Bash” Croft ultimately emerged as the two winners. The pair shared an £83,000 charity prize after the contestants banished the last two traitors, Maya Jama and King Kenny. Their winnings will be divided between two refugee charities, the Refugee Council and Choose Love. Kenny had reached the endgame, the final stage, by turning on his fellow traitor Maya at the last round table. Singer James Blunt joined Kenny, Romesh and Bash in the endgame, where the group had to decide whether any traitors were left. When a vote left Kenny and James tied, Bash convinced Romesh to banish Kenny, thereby securing victory for the faithful contestants. James could also have won if he had chosen to end the game, but his decision to hold another vote led to his own eviction. The series also featured two unorthodox confessions, with traitors revealing their own identities before being swiftly removed by the others. Richard E Grant blurted out his secret role in the second episode because he was so excited to have been selected. James Acaster, described in the report as the programme's most reluctant traitor, gave himself up under pressure during Thursday's penultimate episode. An apparently misplaced reaction shot fuelled speculation about how heavily the round-table scene had been edited. The report suggested that Acaster's confession revived the programme after what some viewers regarded as a mid-series lull. More than 15 million people had been watching the series. A Hollywood Reporter article contrasted record-breaking ratings with a perceived consensus on social media that the series had been rather dull. Some viewers pointed to a shortage of double-crossing and explosive arguments, describing the celebrities as more friendly and strategically aware than earlier groups. The drama intensified in the final, which the report suggested was likely to have been the year's most watched television programme.
